subject: Biology
title: Habitats and Niches
description: A quick win: understand Habitats and Niches.

hook.text: A habitat is where an organism lives. A niche is how it lives there—its job in the ecosystem.

buildup.text: Two species can share a habitat but not a niche. Competition drives one out over time.

discovery.text: The competitive exclusion principle says no two species can occupy the same niche indefinitely.

twist.text: Darwin's finches evolved different beak shapes to exploit different food niches on the same islands.

climax.text: Niche partitioning allows many species to coexist by dividing resources in creative ways.

punchline.text: Same address, different jobs. That's coexistence.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a habitat and a niche?
options: Habitat is where; niche is how it lives there
Habitat is food; niche is shelter

details.summary: A habitat is the physical environment where an organism lives, while its niche encompasses its total role including what it eats, when it is active, and how it interacts with other species. The niche concept explains how multiple species share the same habitat.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding niches explains biodiversity patterns and how species coexist. When niches overlap too much, competition drives exclusion or adaptation. Niche theory guides conservation by identifying what resources species truly need to survive.
takeaways: A niche includes all biotic and abiotic conditions a species requires
The fundamental niche is broader than the realized niche shaped by competition
Species coexist by occupying different niches within shared habitats

faq.question: What is the difference between a habitat and a niche?
faq.answer: A habitat is the physical place an organism lives, like a coral reef or forest floor. A niche is the organism's ecological role, including what it eats, when it is active, where it nests, and how it interacts with other species within that habitat.

faq.question: Why is the realized niche smaller than the fundamental niche?
faq.answer: The fundamental niche includes all conditions where a species could survive. Competition, predation, and other interactions restrict it to the realized niche, the narrower range it actually occupies. Remove competitors, and species often expand toward their fundamental niche.
